Bob Havens was born in Quincy, Illinois on May 3, 1930. He showed an early aptitude for music, studying the violin and piano and eventually excelling on the trombone. He cites his visit to New Orleans in 1956 as an important career move, one which led to a four year stint with trumpeter Al Hirt. Bob has had important roles with two American institutions, Lawrence Welk and Disneyland.

He spent 22 years with the Welk Orchestra and was often the featured trombonist on the TV show. He also found time to perform traditional jazz with Sharkey Bonono and Armand Hug. Bob currently performs with the Lawrence Welk production in Branford, Missouri and is a familiar guest at jazz parties around the country.
Bob was interviewed at the Allegheny Jazz Party in Chautauqua, New York on September 12, 1997 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We are filming today in Chautauqua, New York for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and my guest today is Bob Havens, trombonist. Welcome.
Well, it’s a pleasure to be here, Monk.
Is it a bit of a challenge to fit this in during this weekend? They have you working pretty hard.
Yes, they have us going a number of times each day, and so I have — well I haven’t counted up the sets but I think it’s like nine or ten sets over a period of about three days.
Somehow jazz at nine AM doesn’t seem quite right.
I’ve always felt that way. I have never liked to play early in the day. My mind just doesn’t get going at full momentum that early.
